npcs.name: Gus

0: Hmph. New in town? Packs are on the wall, prices are on the tag, and no, I don't do haggling.
Don't bend the cards. I can hear it when you bend the cards.
Coffee's free if you're buying. Coffee's also free if you're not. Just don't tell anyone.
2: You're getting the hang of this. Sleeve your rares, kid. Trust me.
Saturday nights we run the Showdown. Bring a deck you believe in.
Thirty years I've run this shop. Still get butterflies opening a fresh box.
4: Fine, fine. You've earned a game against the old binder deck. Don't cry when the dragon shows up.
Ever seen a First-Edition Kindling Fox? I pulled one in '94, back when Sparkfolk was new. Sold it to pay rent. Biggest regret of my life.
If you ever want to pick up a shift, the register could use someone who can count.
6: This shop feels a little less empty with you around. Don't make it weird.
You know what this game's really about? It's the people at the table. Always was.

npcs.battle_intro: Alright, shuffle up. And cut my deck like you mean it.
win_lines: Hah! Good game. You've got a real feel for it, kid.
lose_lines: Dragon gets everybody eventually. Go again?

npcs.name: Mira

0: You're the new one, right? I'm Mira. I've won the last four Showdowns. Just so you know.
Tempo is everything. Use every Spark, every turn. Don't let them breathe.
Morning runs, afternoon testing. That's the routine.
2: Not bad, not bad. Your curve is still a mess, though.
Thirty cards, three copies of everything that's good. That's the whole secret.
I lose sometimes, you know. I just don't like it.
4: Want my sideboard notes? ...Okay, just the first page.
Honestly? Playing you is more fun than playing the regulars. Don't let it go to your head.
6: When regionals come around, we're road-tripping. I already decided.
Thanks for not treating me like the scary tryhard. I kind of am, but still.

npcs.battle_intro: Fine. One game. Try to keep up.
win_lines: ...Okay. That was a good line. I'll remember it.

npcs.name: Nana Rose

0: Oh, hello dear! I don't play to win, I play for the pretty pictures. Look at this hen!
My late husband collected these. Now I do. Forty-two binders and counting.
Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten.
2: I made a binder just for the bird cards. Is that silly? It's not silly.
Gus pretends to be grumpy, but he gave me a free pack on my birthday. Every year.
4: I set aside a little something for you, dear. Don't tell the children.
You remind me of him, you know. The way your eyes light up at a shiny card.
6: When I'm gone, I want my binders to go to someone who'll love them. I think I know who.
Come by any time. The kettle's always on.

npcs.battle_intro: Oh, a game? How lovely. Go easy on an old woman. Or don't, I don't mind.
win_lines: Well done, sweetheart! Here, have a cookie with your coins.
lose_lines: Oh my, did I win? The hens did all the work.

npcs.name: Pip

0: Do you have any DRAGONS? I don't have any dragons. My mom says packs are a 'treat'.
My deck has a STAG. It has SIX POWER. Do you know what six power means? It means it's HUGE.
Tilly says hedgehogs are the best creature type. Tilly is RIGHT.
2: You're like, really good. Can you teach me what a 'sideboard' is? Is it a board? On the side?
I pulled a shiny! It's a shiny badger! Look!!
4: When I grow up I'm gonna own a card shop. You can work there. For free.
You're my favorite grown-up. Don't tell my mom.
6: I saved up all week. Wanna open a pack together? You can have the rare. Maybe.

npcs.battle_intro: BATTLE! I'm gonna STOMP you! Respectfully!
win_lines: Aww man. That was SO cool though. Rematch tomorrow!

npcs.name: Judge Theo

0: Theo. Level two judge. If you ever have a rules question, I have an answer. Usually with a citation.
Fresh creatures can't attack the turn they're played - unless they're Swift. They still guard their lane, though.
Fun fact: a Soar creature flies right over the lane, unless the creature across also Soars.
2: The community center used to host regionals. Maybe it will again, if someone fixes the roof.
Shield stops the first hit. Any hit. Even from a dragon. Pop it with something small first.
4: I don't play favorites. But if I did, hypothetically, you'd be on the list.
Between you and me: Mira's deck folds to a crab in every lane. You didn't hear it from a judge.
6: I'm thinking of running a draft night. I'd want you there. As a player, and as a friend.

npcs.battle_intro: A friendly game. I'll call my own triggers.
win_lines: Clean play. No infractions. Well done.
lose_lines: Good game. You missed a lethal on turn six, by the way.

npcs.name: Corwin

0: Oh. You collect too? How quaint. I have a complete Hearthvale set. Graded.
Pack odds are a scam, by the way. I buy singles like a civilized person.
Don't touch the display case. Gus and I have an understanding.
2: Your binder is... not terrible. Who taught you to sort by color? Correct, by the way.
I'm still hunting a First-Edition Fox. If you ever pull one... we should talk.
4: Fine. You're a real collector. I admit it. Don't make me say it twice.
Want to see my secret rares? You're the first person I've shown.
6: I used to collect because I wanted to be the only one with the rare stuff. Now I mostly want someone to show it to.

npcs.battle_intro: If you insist. Try not to bend my sleeves.
lose_lines: As expected. Better cards, better results.
